snippet.textDisplay:
I think it’s just an identity crisis, gta6 is a good game (hindered by its obsession with visuals over performance) but it’s becomes less of a GTA game about the GTA formula and is now more of a relationship virtual reality game with a sprinkling of crime to keep somewhat tied to the name.. I

If it had been released as a separate game like SIMs direct control, then it would be beloved and a masterpiece, but what we have is a game that released to glowing 10s, sponsorships with Google, discord, twitch, consoles and beyond all in one swoop.. it generated skepticism, not acceptance.. and when people walk into a perfect house, after being told a house is perfect, they’re looking for the flaws and something to pick apart.. 

GTA 6 is a good game, not perfect, and doesn’t feel like a GTA game.. it feels like red dead redemption 2 in the modern era with a boring protagonist and his partner + crime.. 

I think it’s generated distrust in reviewers we already don’t trust, distrust in the larger media space and distrust in companies we thought we knew (people honestly forget that rockstar allowed that god awful remaster of San Andreas, and their insane approach to leakers/hackers) 

I’ll be glad when the hype behind gta6 dies off completely and games can go back to being fun, rather than visual overhauls with “controls”

17:33 right, but this is the bare minimum. Doing just that will only match my expectations and I always expect a good game (7/10) with those expectations scaling relative to budget, time, manpower, all of which are also tied to the studio’s prior releases.

Them copy pasting the RDR2 mechanics and shit from 2004 isn’t going to earn them any points from me, it won’t subtract any but it won’t earn any either. Nor will a slight upgrade to those copy pasted mechanics because that’s just an iterative improvement, not an evolution which again shouldn’t be applauded as anything great.

It’s good it’s there, but it should be there. And so far from everything I’ve seen, it’s at least a 7/10 based on that principle with everything else like the story, side content and monetisation either pushing it up or down from that point.

And in that regard it just does look like it’ll be an 8/10 overall objectively speaking. Which is still an amazing game. It’s just not a masterpiece and it doesn’t have to be to still find enjoyment in it.

snippet.textDisplay:
I agree on most things... but as someone who never cared for RDR2 because of its setting and slow pace (never cared for American Western stuff)... yeah, it's quite clear how much GTA 6 takes from RDR2. And yeah, we'll see. I'm not much of a fan of slow-burn games like that. I guess it really is a matter of taste.
Hard to say... I don't want to complain, but I don't like RDR2 mechanics sliding into GTA... mostly because I didn't like RDR2. It has nothing to do with the quality of the game. I just never cared for a slow-burn American Western where we do the whole frontier thing and talk about feelings and whatnot. I know the game is a masterpiece... but I just didn't enjoy it.

GTA 6 so far is 50/50 for me. I enjoy it... but some aspects of hyperrealism and the systems copied from RDR2 are not really my thing.

That being said, I'm like 16 hours in, and it does get a bit more fun as it goes on, so maybe it gets better.
My very first impression was "WOW, THIS IS INCREDIBLE", followed by "OK, can we move on a bit faster?"
